notes: Access: Claude-in-Chrome only, one dedicated tab. robots.txt (https://www.nitori-net.jp/robots.txt) names no Claude/anthropic agent - only generic query-string disallows plus a Google-CloudVertexBot rule - so extraction is permitted. Tree source: the full category sitemap https://www.nitori-net.jp/ecstatic/sitemap/sitemap_item_1.xml (1,594 entries, 818 distinct /ec/cat/ paths after dropping ?brands= filter variants, across 36 top-level departments). I then crawled the tree breadth-first with same-origin fetch() from the loaded page, parsing each page's <script id="nitoristore-state"> SSR blob - 529 category nodes retrieved, 0 errors, no block of any kind. Each node's own children came from that blob's 'sub-categories'.categories array (code + Japanese name + pathUrl), which is the site's own tile strip, so the nav, sitemap and per-page child list were reconciled into one union. Counts: qty = cx-state.product.search.results.pagination.totalResults from that same SSR blob. This is NOT a third-party count API - it is the exact number the storefront prints as its 'N件' listing header. Corroborated in two regimes by rendering the pages in the tab: Console Tables printed '5件' vs totalResults 5, and Fabric Sofas printed '431件' vs totalResults 431. Trap checks: (2) bad slugs - Sofa/ThisSlugDoesNotExistXYZ and TableChair/BogusNodeQQQ both return HTTP 200 but with NO state blob and NO h1, never a parent's number, so this platform does not serve plausible wrong counts; every emitted leaf was additionally confirmed to carry an h1 matching the node requested. (3) node identity was keyed on the URL slug throughout, never the label - needed here because Nitori repeats labels across departments (e.g. 'オフィススツール' appears as OfficeChairStool 22 and ReceptionRoomSofaStoolSofa 28) and because slugs lie (OutdoorTravel/Outdoortent is labelled 'Outdoor Chairs & Tables'). (4) counts drifted 0 across the session on re-read. Cross-listed mirror nodes: Nitori duplicates categories across departments with an m1/m2 code prefix and a DIFFERENT (smaller) product count - e.g. Chair/StoolFloordinin 83 vs Sofa/m1StoolFloordinin 67; Sofa/Sofabed 66 vs Bed/m1Sofabed 54; TableChair/BedSideNightTable 133 vs Bed/m1BedSideNightTable 108; StudyDeskChildRoom/StudyChair 46 vs Chair/m1StudyChair 40. I kept only the canonical node in its home department and dropped every m-prefixed mirror, to avoid double-counting. Excluded whole departments after inspection: StorageRackDresser (収納ケース - clothing cases, storage boxes, baskets, hangers, compression bags: standalone storage goods, not furniture); Mattress (bedding per brief); Shingu (futon/bedding); Pet (incl. its 'ペット家具' pet-furniture node); RelaxHealth, SeniorGoods, Appliance, Lighting_Fixture, InteriorLifeGoods (decor/mirrors/candles), BathToiletLaundry (towels, bath stools, shower racks - no vanity units or bathroom furniture anywhere in it), CarpetRugMat, Cushion, CurtainRailBlind, Tableware, KitchenGoodsTableware, Roomwear, Laundry. Excluded individual nodes: Baby/BabyBed (93) - title scan showed it is overwhelmingly baby futons, sheets and mattress pads with only a couple of actual cribs; StudyDeskChildRoom/KidsShingu (29) - pure kids bedding; all Kotatsu futon/cover branches; all sofa/chair/zaisu covers and maintenance items; Chair/SimpleTableChairStool (踏み台, step stools); Storage-Furniture/HangarRack/WallHangarDoorhangar (wall and door hangers, hardware); OfficeBookshelfStationery/Bookshelf/BookshelfParts and ColorBox parts nodes (components); TvStandLivingStorage/butsudan (Buddhist altars and ritual goods); TvStandLivingStorage magazine/remote racks; LifeSuppliesDailyNecessities/Entrancegoods shoe and slipper racks (small entryway accessories - the furniture shoe cabinets are already covered by Storage-Furniture/EntranceStorage/ShoesBox 71); Laundry/ShelfStrutRackRack (over-washer laundry racks, utility fixtures); Houjin office information boards, artificial greenery, office accessories and safes; Baby gates and playpens. Feature/collection pages with a null count were skipped per the never-extract rule: f1bed-combine, f1ncollection, f1/f2/f3/f4Orderstorage, f1wallstorage, f2wallstorage, f1middleboardporte, f1kitchenboardcombine. Top buckets: 'Furniture' for the consumer tree; 'Outdoor Furniture' for the two garden/outdoor nodes; and 'Office Furniture' for the Houjin (オフィス家具・法人) B2B department, which the site itself names Office Furniture and which is a genuinely separate 1,798-product catalogue.
